text:
maria: quick flag — observed double token accounting for a streaming session after a routing rebalance this morning. client: app-prod-42, session: sess_9a2f, request_id: r_71bd. ledger shows provisional tokens + final confirmed tokens both applied.

sam: can you paste the raw event ids from the router/ledger?

maria: log snippet:```
[router] route_change: from pool-a -> pool-b, reason=rebalance, session=sess_9a2f
[stream] stream_resume: client_ack=true, toolcall=null, prefix_tokens=120
[ledger] provisional_charge: +120 tokens, final_charge: +120 tokens
```

oliver: ugh. sounds similar to a handoff race where provisional was never cleared on successful finalization. which routing policy was in use?

maria: policy=affinity_prefer, fallback=balanced. we had a transient shard drain so router moved session mid-stream.

jun: did the runtime emit a close/commit event to ledger with the same provisional id? sometimes id mapping fails on multi-hop.

maria: ledger shows two different ids: prov=prov_1182, final=final_773. timestamps within 1s. client only saw one success.

lisa: is this involving a tool call? toolcalls create extra accounting paths because the tool server can truncate or resend suffix tokens.
maria: no toolcall in this trace, plain streaming generate. but the stream was truncated at the rejoin point and resumed from a different node.

ryan: possible root causes: router replayed prefix to new node causing a provisional on new node while old provisional never received the ack to clear. or ledger dedupe key uses node-local ids.

sam: can you grep for `dedupe_key` in runtime and ledger traces? We should confirm whether dedupe uses session+offset or event uuid.
maria: grep results attached in case log:```
runtime: dedupe_key=session:sess_9a2f:offset:120
ledger: dedupe_key=event_uuid:prov_1182
```

oliver: there it is — mismatch in dedupe semantics. runtime uses session+offset, ledger expects event_uuid. during handoff the event_uuid changed. ledger treats it as new charge.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T09:12 completed for router-hotfix/v12 -> rolled to 60%.

jun: short-term mitigation: make ledger accept either dedupe key (union) or add a reconciliation that maps session+offset -> event_uuid when available. long-term: unify dedupe key contract in the internal API.

lisa: console UX question — should we show provisional vs confirmed token lines in the per-session timeline? Ops wants to see provisional items flagged so they can tell which charges might be rolled back.

ryan: +1 for visible provisional line. also add tooltip: "Provisional tokens are recorded at handoff and may be reconciled on session finalize."

sam: agree. also we need a dashboard alert for sudden provisional spikes per router. this will catch rebalances causing dupe provisional charges.

maria: another edge: client resumed with `resume_offset` that overlapped by 1 token because of off-by-one in prefix trim. when runtime replayed it counted 1 extra token. so combination of dedupe mismatch + off-by-one truncation caused full duplication.

oliver: we should add a unit test that simulates: handoff -> offset overlap -> different event_uuid. expect ledger to not double charge.

jun: I can own the ledger change to accept fallback dedupe keys and add reconciliation. ETA EOW for a spec PR.

lisa: I'll file a console ticket to add provisional/confirmed toggles and a small query to surface provisional spikes per router.

sam: temporary ops playbook: run one-time reconciliation job to find sessions with provisional+final within 5s and same client/session and refund provisional duplicates. billing-bot: can you create a provisional refund runbook?

billing-bot: created billing task BT-2026-153. assigned to @billing-team. scheduled window tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

maria: thanks. action items: (1) jun spec PR for ledger dedupe union, (2) oliver unit test added to runtime handoff suite, (3) lisa console ticket for provisional visibility, (4) billing team runbook. marking owner tags in doc.

sam: and let's add a short telemetry metric: `provisional_to_final_ratio` per router and an alert when >1.5 for 5m. saves us the next wakeup call. :+1:
